page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on KVM virtualization and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The instance supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by 256 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Cache provisioning includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI for vector math and cryptographic operations. Hardware accelerators are omitted with a zero GPU count, and no bundled local storage is provided, requiring external network block storage for persistence. Network connectivity is rated at a 32 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory subsystems, placing its multi-core stress-ng score of 62,017.14 and Geekbench multi-core score of 16,705 in the top 25% of measured systems. Multi-threaded compilation under Clang reached 40,694, and PassMark database operations reached 25,157.94, both representing upper-quartile outputs. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect average performance, evidenced by a single-core Geekbench score of 1,603.0 and stress-ng single-core throughput of 1,848.79. Large uncached memory reads achieved 169.75 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measured 42.67 GB/sec, placing overall input/output and single-threaded operations in the middle 50% tier.

The 64 vCPU scale offers strong resource density for parallel tasks, but workloads reliant on low-latency local disk must account for the lack of onboard storage. The instance delivers solid qualitative cost efficiency for highly concurrent backends, distributed build farms, enterprise microservices, intermediate data transformations, and high-concurrency database servers.

Utilizing an x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading across 32 physical cores, it features AVX-512 vector extensions, cryptographic accelerators, and 32 Gbps baseline networking. The system contains no integrated local storage or GPU hardware, relying on external block storage for data persistence. Benchmark results indicate top-quartile multi-core compute and compilation speeds, alongside average single-core execution and memory streaming rates.
